meta.title: Cultural journeys with Indonesia's indigenous communities
meta.description: Join ceremonies, learn traditional crafts, cook in village kitchens and walk with local hosts from Bali and Java to Papua.

hero.eyebrow: Cultural travel, led by local hosts
hero.description: Small journeys into Indonesia's customary villages. Join a ceremony, learn to weave, cook in a family kitchen and hear the stories no guidebook has written down.

categories.title: Choose how you want to know Indonesia

featured.title: The journeys people remember
featured.description: Small groups, guides from the community itself, and schedules that follow the rhythm of the village rather than the other way round.

destinations.title: From lakeside temples to villages above the sea

local.title: Led by local hosts
local.body: Every tour is led by someone from the community itself: temple priests, weavers, fishermen or village cooks.

small.title: Small groups
small.body: A dozen or so travellers per departure at most, so visits never overwhelm daily village life.

fair.title: Fair revenue sharing
fair.body: Most of what you pay goes directly to the host families and customary groups.

respect.title: Respect for custom
respect.body: We brief you on etiquette before you go: what to wear, when photos are welcome and how to take part politely.

story.title: Morning in the Subak, when water is shared with prayer
story.body: Before sunrise the pekaseh opens the sluice and lays an offering at the edge of the dyke. The subak system has governed Bali's rice fields since the 11th century, and it still works because its people still believe in it. On our journey you don't just look at terraces. You walk behind the farmers who keep them.
story.quote: The water isn't mine. My job is only to share it.
story.quoteAuthor: A saying among the pekaseh of Subak Tegallalang
story.imageAlt: Tegallalang rice terraces in the morning
